notes: ACCESS: direct curl_cffi fetch via probe.py; HTTP 200 on every request across chrome124/chrome131/safari17_2_ios/safari18_0/firefox133/chrome120. No WAF, no proxy, no reader service - matching the Furniture-pass ledger. ROBOTS: https://fermliving.us/robots.txt fetched FIRST, before any other request. It is 48 bytes in total and reads, in full: 'User-agent: *' / 'Disallow: */pages/configurator?*=*'. There is NO group naming anthropic-ai, ClaudeBot, Claude-Web, Claude-SearchBot or any Claude agent, no wildcard Disallow, no Crawl-delay and no Content-Signal line. The single disallowed pattern (*/pages/configurator?*=*) was never requested; every URL touched is a bare /collections/<handle>, /collections/<handle>/products.json, /collections.json or /pages/the-bathroom. probe.py's 2s per-host gap was honoured throughout. TREE: taken verbatim from the rendered mega-menu in the homepage HTML. There are FOUR mega-menu menu-points (data-megamenu-menu-point): 'Shop', 'Rooms', 'Inspiration', 'Professionals'. The Shop mega-menu is the entire product taxonomy - a static column (Gift Guides, Ferm Living Classics, Shop by Series, Bestsellers, News, Kids News) plus 10 departments in data-dynamic-menu-parent blocks whose children sit in matching data-dynamic-menu-child blocks: Kids, Outdoor Living, Accessories, Furniture, Sofas, Lighting, Kitchen, Textiles, Rugs, Certified Products. I dumped all 10 department child lists in full (78 distinct /collections/ hrefs on the homepage). NOT ONE of the 10 departments is Bathroom/Bath, and no department has a Bathroom child. The Rooms mega-menu (data-megamenu-type='rooms_megamenu') is NOT a taxonomy - it is 8 image tiles pointing at /pages/ editorial lookbooks: the-living-room, the-dining-room, the-kitchen, the-hallway, the-bathroom, the-bedroom, the-kids-room, the-office. I fetched /pages/the-bathroom (HTTP 200, 460KB): it has NO h1, no product-count element and no product grid of its own - it is a styled lookbook whose only outbound shopping links are 20 individual /products/ PDPs plus /collections/the-bathroom-see-what-is-coming and /collections/the-sama-collection. UNIVERSE CHECK: I enumerated the store's ENTIRE collection list at /collections.json?limit=250 paged to exhaustion - 182 collections, single page, no page 2 - and grepped every handle and title for bath|shower|toilet|soap|towel|vanity|basin|sink|mirror|wc|sanitary|hook|holder|brush|faucet|tap. The complete hit list is: the-bathroom (33), the-bathroom-see-what-is-coming (26), shower-curtains (9), towels (16), mirrors (28), hooks-and-holders (55), candleholders (55), holiday-candles (41). Nothing else bathroom-related exists anywhere in the store, hidden from the nav or otherwise. CONFIRMED ABSENT: ferm LIVING US sells NO bathroom fixtures or sanitaryware whatsoever - across the full 182-collection universe and all four mega-menus there is no Baths/Bathtubs, Basins/Sinks, Toilets/WCs, Bidets, Showers, Shower Enclosures/Screens/Doors, Bathroom Taps/Faucets/Mixers, Vanity Unit or Bathroom Storage/Cabinet node at any depth. It is a Danish design homeware brand. Its genuine bath-accessory products DO exist (Mist soap dishes/toothbrush holders/cotton pad holders, Bon soap tray/toothbrush holder, Ceramic soap trays, Sama toilet brushes/soap dispensers/toilet paper dispensers, Curvature toilet paper holders/towel hangers, Dora towel shelves/stand) but the storefront gives them NO bathroom listing URL of their own - they are merchandised inside Accessories > Small Storage and Accessories > Hooks and Holders, which are general accessory nodes, and surfaced only via the room lookbook and the design-series edits. Per rules 2, 24 and 25 there is therefore no valid Bathroom leaf to record, so rows is empty and all eight findings are documented in review. QTY METHOD (used for the review figures, none of which are recorded as rows): this Shopify theme renders NO product-count header on any collection page - verified by stripping the full rendered HTML of /collections/towels to plain text, which goes h1 'Towels' -> sort control -> product grid -> pagination with no total anywhere, exactly as the Furniture-pass ledger recorded. Counts therefore come from enumeration by TWO independent routes: (a) paging the rendered collection HTML (?page=N) to exhaustion and counting unique /products/<handle> slugs, and (b) /collections/<handle>/products.json?limit=250 paged to exhaustion and counted by unique product id. VERIFICATION: the two routes agree exactly on all four leaves tested across four different sizes - towels 16/16 (2 pages), shower-curtains 9/9 (2 pages), mirrors 28/28 (2 pages), hooks-and-holders 55/55 (3 pages). They also agree with collections.json products_count on this storefront for every handle checked (16/9/28/55/152/33/26), i.e. the Shopify products_count inflation trap did not bite here, but products_count was still not used as the source. The one disagreement is /collections/the-bathroom, where the crude rendered-HTML slug scan returns 62 against products.json's 33; that page cross-sells the 26-product 'see what is coming' edit in a secondary block, so the grid-scoped products.json figure (33) is the one reported. DISCRIMINATION: 9, 16, 26, 28, 33, 38, 44, 55, 152 - no site-wide constant. H1/CANONICAL: /collections/towels returns h1 'Towels' and is self-canonical (rel=canonical https://fermliving.us/collections/towels), confirming the node requested is the node served. CROSS-FILE DEDUP: lib/dedup.already_extracted() was run on all 13 candidate URLs (the-bathroom, the-bathroom-see-what-is-coming, mirrors, hooks-and-holders, small-storage, towels, shower-curtains, accessories, textiles, bags-and-baskets, storage, shelves, mats-and-runners). Two hits, both Furniture.xlsx for this same company - /collections/storage as 'Storage' and /collections/shelves as 'Shelves' - and neither is a bathroom node, so neither would have been a Bathroom candidate anyway. The remaining 11 returned None. Note the index holds 17 fermliving.us Furniture rows and 20 fermliving.com Home-Decor rows; because the earlier Home Decor pass ran on the .com sibling domain, fermliving.us/collections/mirrors is NOT a dedup hit even though fermliving.com/collections/mirrors is recorded in Final.xlsx as 'Mirrors'. Nothing was removed from rows for dedup - rows was empty on classification grounds first. DOMAIN: everything here comes from fermliving.us itself (HTTP 200 direct, not a redirect); its locale switcher lists fermliving.com, fermliving.co.uk, fermliving.dk and fermliving.se as separate sibling storefronts, and nothing was taken from any of them.
